title: api: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency, retry-after and error codes across OpenAI compat layer and streaming
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Unifies rate-limit semantics and error codes exposed by the OpenAI compatibility layer. Adds idempotency-key support and clearer Retry-After handling for streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Backwards-compatible defaults preserved; opt-in strict mode available via header.
description:
Motivation:
Redwood's OpenAI-compat API surface had historically mixed behaviors for rate-limits, idempotency, and streaming error semantics across the hosted API and private deployments. Customers integrating with both the native Redwood endpoints and the OpenAI-compat layer saw inconsistent Retry-After handling, differing HTTP status codes for transient vs hard errors, and no unified idempotency semantics for non-chat endpoints. These inconsistencies increase developer cognitive load and lead to brittle retry logic in customers' SDKs.

What this PR does (summary):
- Standardizes rate-limit semantics across the API (409 -> 429 mapping, Retry-After header semantics), aligning with OpenAI compat expectations while preserving Redwood internal signals.
- Adds first-class idempotency-key support for generation endpoints (both streaming and non-streaming) with deterministic error behavior and idempotency table TTLs.
- Stabilizes streaming failure behavior: streaming now emits a final error frame with consistent JSON error shape and includes a Retry-After suggestion when appropriate.
- Introduces a small compatibility shim that maps Redwood internal error codes to the OpenAI-compatible error codes (and documents the mapping).
- Adds an opt-in strict-compat header (X-Redwood-Compat: openai-strict) for customers who want exact OpenAI semantics; default remains backward-compatible Redwood semantics with improved consistency.

Detailed changes (high level):
- runtime/api/compat/openai_error_map.go: mapping table and tests for error code mappings.
- runtime/api/handler/rate_limit.go: centralizes rate-limiting logic and ensures 429 is returned for tenant-level throttling; earlier 409 responses are mapped.
- runtime/api/handler/idempotency.go: idempotency key validation, storage hooks, and deterministic response replay for completed idempotent requests.
- runtime/api/streaming/stream_writer.go: final error frame shape and Retry-After header support for streaming transports (chunked and SSE).
- redwood-docs/docs/api/error-codes.md: doc updates with examples and migration notes.
- redwood-sdk-python: minor client helper added to surface Retry-After parsing and idempotency-key convenience.

Checklist:
- [x] Add centralized rate-limit mapping and tests
- [x] Add idempotency implementation and unit/integration tests
- [x] Stabilize streaming error frames and add e2e test that validates client retry behavior
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat docs and SDK helper
- [x] Add migration notes and rollout plan

Compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior is backward-compatible: previously accepted requests still work, but clients will see more consistent error codes and Retry-After headers.
- The new X-Redwood-Compat: openai-strict header enables exact OpenAI mapping for customers migrating from OpenAI and expecting identical semantics.
- Gradual rollout planned: feature-flagged behind ff/error-handling-unify; initial rollout to staging then canary to 5% internal customers before full rollout.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for error mappings and idempotency table eviction.
- Integration tests that validate streaming final frames and Retry-After propagation through proxies.
- Manual QA: exercised against redwood-compat-e2e infra; SDK integration test validates automatic inclusion/validation of idempotency-key for non-streaming gen endpoints.

Migration notes for customers:
- If you rely on previous 409 semantics for quota vs rate-limit, switch to checking both 409/429 for a short transition window or opt-in to openai-strict.
- To use idempotency semantics, include Idempotency-Key header; clients using SDK helpers will set this automatically when calling with retry helpers.
- README and release notes updated with examples.

Related work:
- ENG-4123: unify API error semantics
- SRE-210: reduce noisy retries and improve rate-limit observability
- SUP-882: customer-reported inconsistent Retry-After - root cause and fix
